messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered: PD#INC-4921 - metrics-pipeline.scrape-job-drop (severity: P1)

pagerduty: Incident INC-4921 created and assigned to #eng-sre on-call. Trigger: prometheus-scrape-job: repeated 5m failures from exporter 'node-exporter-prod' (region-us-east-1).

alex: acked. I'm oncall, taking this. seeing scrape errors in grafana alert details.

maria: :eyes: pinging ingest team too — last successful scrape around 1818231200, then gaps. any recent deploys to exporters?

jon: I didn't deploy anything in that cluster. kafka consumer for log-ingest shows a spike in lag at ~1818231000, could be backpressure.

alex: looking at prometheus targets: `up{job="node-exporter",instance=~".*us-east-.*"}` - a bunch of `down` for exporter pods. One node shows connection refused.

alex: tailing exporter pod logs:
```
kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/node-exporter-us-east-1 --since=15m
# output: tcp accept failed: too many open files
# repeated OOM-ish messages and connection resets
```

maria: that sounds like file-descriptor exhaustion on the exporter. Could be related to log-rotate or recent increase in scrape frequency. running `ss -s` on the host?

jon: checking node metrics: sockets in TIME_WAIT high, FD usage at 92%. Also noticed kernel dmesg with `conntrack: table full` messages earlier.

alex: immediate mitigation steps — reduce prometheus scrape concurrency for node-exporter to avoid further fd exhaustion. From runbook: edit prometheus scrape config and reduce `scrape_interval` and `concurrency` for node-exporter job.

alex: applying temporary override via configmap rollout: `kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-scrape --patch '{"data":{"node-exporter_scrape_concurrency":"2"}}'` — applying now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update applied to prometheus-config.

pagerduty: Update: config change applied. Will keep monitoring.

maria: also bumping node-exporter replicaCount from 2 -> 4 in us-east to spread connections while we stabilize. Applying helm patch now.

jon: note: log-ingest kafka consumer lag reduced after config change? looks like lag started to drop ~5m after throttling scrapes. might be upstream pressure easing.

alex: checking customer impact — platform metrics show increased 5xxs for /v1/embeddings endpoint between 1818230800-1818232200. Peak 5xx rate ~1.8% — likely transient but might have hit a few critical jobs.

maria: billing-alerts: a couple of customers reported slow ingestion but no widespread alerts in support. I'll open a post-incident customer note if P1 continues.

jon: running additional health checks:
```
# verify exporter endpoints
for ip in $(kubectl -n monitoring get endpoints node-exporter-us-east -o jsonpath='{.subsets[*].addresses[*].ip}'); do curl -sS http://$ip:9100/metrics | head -n1 || echo "bad $ip"; done
```

alex: one host still returning connection refused. filed a node-side ticket to infra to check ulimit and conntrack settings. tagging @sre-lead for escalation if we can't recover quickly.

sre-lead: on it. i'll get infra to increase ulimit and bump conntrack table temporarily. also want a timeline for handoff. how long until stable?

alex: current plan: monitoring for 15m after config change, if stable we'll resolve the PD and close the incident. If exporter pods still flapping, escalate-runbook -> infra reboot of the node.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: reminder to ack or escalate if no update in 10m.

maria: cleanup tasks queued: check prom scrape headrooms, add rate limit in prometheus config for that job, add alert for fd usage on exporters. I'll create two follow-ups.

jon: quick note: logs show `too many open files` originating from a recent version of node-exporter with an fd leak bug. recommend pinning back to previous image after stabilization.

alex: good find. moving to pin image to v1.2.3 temporarily. rolling update initiated.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for node-exporter -> image=node-exporter:v1.2.3

pagerduty: INC-4921 status: acknowledged by alex, severity P1. Escalation policy will notify on-call infra if not resolved in 20m.

maria: monitoring graphs: scrape success ratio back to normal in us-east after rollout and concurrency reduction. still one host with intermittent connection refused but most targets are green.

alex: preparing short incident summary for handoff before my shift ends in 35m. Key points: root cause suspected node-exporter fd leak in v1.3.0, mitigation: reduced scrape concurrency and pinned exporter to v1.2.3, temporary replica bump. Customer impact: brief 1-2% 5xx spike on embeddings endpoint for ~20m, limited reports. Next steps: infra to verify node ulimits/conntrack + patch exporter image in stable channel, add fd-usage alert, do RCA.

sre-lead: thanks, team. if it remains stable after 15m, we'll resolve INC-4921 and create a follow-up RFC for exporter image gating. If it regresses, escalate to infra and consider rolling nodes.

alex: handing off to `ingest-oncall` for overnight coverage. ingest-oncall, ping when you've taken over and I'll DM a short runbook + commands I ran.

ingest-oncall: taking over. thanks alex — i'll watch for any PD re-triggers and confirm infra actions in the morning. I've got the command list and runbook.

pagerduty: INC-4921: acknowledged -> assigned to ingest-oncall.

incident-bot: Reminder: please paste a short summary + timeline when closing the incident.

ingest-oncall: will do. closing notes planned: cause, mitigations, customer impact, follow-ups (RCA, image pin, alerts).

alex: thanks all, good job coordinating. :thumbsup:
